display.purpose: Page titles only, via the shared page header; light, tight, 34px phone / 46px desktop.

headline.purpose: Dialog titles and the lead heading inside a section.

stat.purpose: Headline numbers in panels (fitness, predictions, PBs); display face, tabular.

body.purpose: All working copy; descriptions capped at 60ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase mono captions directly above a value, and table column headers. Never an eyebrow above a heading.

figure.purpose: Units, dates, paces, count superscripts and meta lines; always tabular.

shadows.name: panel-drop
shadows.purpose: Every panel; long, soft, nearly invisible lift.

shadows.name: panel-glow
shadows.purpose: Signal light rising behind a panel's top edge (::before); cross-fades to 0.26/0.08 on hover over 0.7s (::after).

shadows.name: lit-pill-on
shadows.value: inset 0 0 1px var(--glow), inset 0 0 10px var(--glow-soft), 0 0 18px var(--glow-soft), 0 0 52px rgba(43, 86, 201, 0.5)
shadows.purpose: Primary pill on hover/focus: current running through it.

shadows.name: point-glow
shadows.purpose: Live dots, active nav dot, status dots; the tab-bar indicator uses 10px.

shadows.name: glass
shadows.purpose: Phone top bar and tab bar only: chrome content scrolls under.

motion.name: ease-signal
motion.purpose: The one easing for every transition (controls 0.3-0.4s, panel glow 0.7s).

motion.name: tick-fade
motion.purpose: Working indicator: three signal dots while the assistant thinks.

motion.name: pulse-ring
motion.purpose: Live dot only; reserved for data that is live now.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All motion stops; the WebGL bloom renders one still frame.

components.css: .ds-panel { font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; position:relative; isolation:isolate; width:300px; padding:24px; border-radius:16px; background:#05070d; color:#e9ecf5; border:1px solid rgba(160,182,235,0.14); box-shadow:0 40px 90px -50px rgba(0,0,0,1); } .ds-panel::before, .ds-panel::after { content:''; position:absolute; inset:0; z-index:-1; border-radius:inherit; pointer-events:none; } .ds-panel::before { background:radial-gradient(9rem 9rem at 50% 0, rgba(141,181,255,0.16), rgba(141,181,255,0.05) 55%, transparent 100%); } .ds-panel::after { background:radial-gradient(9rem 9rem at 50% 0, rgba(141,181,255,0.26), rgba(141,181,255,0.08) 55%, transparent 100%); opacity:0; transition:opacity .7s cubic-bezier(0.6, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-panel:hover::after { opacity:1; } .ds-panel-title { margin:0 0 8px; font-size:15px; font-weight:600; } .ds-row { display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:baseline; padding:12px 0; border-top:1px solid rgba(160,182,235,0.09); } .ds-cap { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size:11px; font-weight:500; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:0.06em; color:#7a819b; } .ds-stat { font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; font-size:26px; font-weight:300; letter-spacing:-0.035em; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; } .ds-stat small { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size:12px; color:#848ba5; letter-spacing:0; }

components.css: .ds-live { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; font-size:12px; color:#848ba5; } .ds-live-dot { position:relative; width:6px; height:6px; border-radius:9999px; color:#8db5ff; background:currentColor; box-shadow:0 0 8px currentColor; } .ds-live-dot::after { content:''; position:absolute; inset:0; border-radius:inherit; background:currentColor; opacity:.5; animation:ds-pulse 2.4s ease-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { from { transform:scale(1); opacity:.5; } to { transform:scale(2.8); opacity:0; } } .ds-ticks { display:inline-flex; gap:4px; margin-left:12px; } .ds-ticks i { width:6px; height:6px; border-radius:9999px; background:#8db5ff; animation:ds-tick 1.2s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-ticks i:nth-child(2) { animation-delay:.2s; } .ds-ticks i:nth-child(3) { animation-delay:.4s; } @keyframes ds-tick { 0%,100% { opacity:.15; } 50% { opacity:1; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-live-dot::after, .ds-ticks i { animation:none; } }

narrative.overview:
Signal is a calm instrument panel for one runner's own data. The ground is deep ink. Panels sit darker than the ground, and a soft signal-blue glow rises behind each panel's top edge. A single cool blue accent marks everything the runner can act on. Display type is a light grotesque set large and tight. Every number, unit and date is set in mono, so data reads like a readout rather than marketing copy. The system was extracted from the user-pinned visual source `frontend/template/redesign-template.html` and adapted to a working app shell. Where the shipped build differs from the template (for example, the panel glow is drawn as a `::before` gradient instead of the template's blurred blob, so panels never clip tooltips), the build is canonical.

There is one look, and it is dark (`color-scheme: dark`). There is no light variant and no theme toggle. Density is moderate: on the phone it supports quick one-handed glances right after a run, and on desktop it holds deeper analysis. Shell chrome stays quiet so the accent stays rare. The system rejects the generic green-on-charcoal SaaS dashboard made of stacked, equal-weight cards.
keyCharacteristics: Deep ink ground with tonal ink layers and blue-tinted alpha hairlines (never neutral greys).
One signal blue for actions, links, active navigation and chart lines.
Green, amber and red appear only as ok, warning and alert states.
Bricolage Grotesque light for display and stat values, Hanken Grotesk for body text, IBM Plex Mono for labels, units, dates and tabular figures.
The glowing panel and the lit pill are the two signature moves.
One easing curve. Motion is slow and quiet, and it stops entirely under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal blue means "you can act here" or "this is live." Do not use it for decoration, section tints or illustration.

rules.name: The Status-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only when a state is ok, warning or alert. Decorative use of a status hue is a defect.

rules.name: The Borrowed Mark Rule
rules.body: Strava orange is the only foreign hue in the UI, and it appears only on Strava-sourced runs.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Components take colour from the `index.css` custom properties through Tailwind's `color-mix` token helper (so `/N` alpha modifiers work). Never write hex in a component.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: If it is a number, unit, date or pace, set it in mono with tabular figures (`.font-mono` is always tabular). If it is prose, never set it in mono.

rules.name: The Light Display Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is always weight 300 with -0.035em tracking. A bold display face is off-system.

rules.name: The Caption-Not-Kicker Rule
rules.body: A mono uppercase label captions a *value* or a table column. It never sits above a heading as an eyebrow.

rules.name: The Kept Shell Rule
rules.body: The desktop sidebar plus the phone tab bar is the navigation. Restyle it, but do not replace it with a hamburger menu or top tabs.

rules.name: The Glass-Where-It-Scrolls Rule
rules.body: Translucent glass (78% panel ink, 18px blur) is only used on chrome that content actually scrolls under or beside: the phone top bar and the phone tab bar.

rules.name: The Light-Not-Lift Rule
rules.body: Elements never translate upward on hover. Interactivity shows as light: the glow brightens, a hairline sharpens, or a wash appears.

rules.name: The Panels-Don't-Clip Rule
rules.body: The panel glow is an isolated pseudo-element, so panels never need `overflow: hidden` and never clip chart tooltips, popovers or focus rings.

dos: Do route every colour through an `index.css` custom property and its Tailwind token. Use `/N` modifiers for alpha.
Do use the lit pill for the one primary action in a view, and quiet outline, ghost or signal pills for everything else.
Do set every number, unit, date and pace in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures. Stat headline values use light Bricolage Grotesque.
Do divide a panel's content into rows with `divider` hairlines, or into ink-2 tiles.
Do pair every status hue with a word or icon.
Do use `ease-signal` for every transition, and check both desktop and about 380px.
donts: Don't put an eyebrow kicker (a small uppercase label) above a heading or page title. Mono uppercase labels caption values and table columns only.
Don't nest a card or panel inside another card or panel. Use hairline-divided rows or ink-2 tiles.
Don't write hex or rgb colour literals in components.
Don't use signal blue as decoration, or green, amber or red for anything but status.
Don't pulse anything that isn't live data, and don't add easings beyond the one curve.
Don't set Bricolage Grotesque heavier than 300, or use it for body copy.
Don't add a light theme or a second accent hue.
